subject: Issues with a Stan-based R package

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Issues with a Stan-based R package
parts:
Hi Stan Developers,

My colleagues and I made a Stan-based R packaged called hBayesDM (GitHub: https://github.com/CCS-Lab, tutorial: rpubs.com/CCSL/hBayesDM). Thanks to feedback form StanCon reviewers, I tried to include precompiled Stan models and follow some of the guidelines for Stan-based R packages (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rstantools/vignettes/developer-guidelines.html). 

Now the latest version (0.3.0) has precompiled models, which run much faster now (thanks!). But there are a few things I could not fix or understand, which are listed below. I think they are related to some C coding or parallel sampling, but I'm not sure. 



1. If I use multiple cores for parallel sampling in RStudio or base R Console, I get the following messages. But if I run the same code in a Mac terminal, I don't have any issues. If I don't use parallel sampling (set 'ncore' to 1), then everything is fine even in RStudio or base R Console. It's very strange to me. 

I opened an issue about this in the hBayesDM GitHub repository and you can see the summary here: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/issues/11


2. There is an error during installation. Please see the following sentences highlighted in red: 

check("hBayesDM", cran = T)

* R * exec * inst * preparing package for lazy loading * help ** installing help indices * building package indices * testing if installed package can be loaded Error in .doLoadActions(where, attach) : error in load action .__A__.1 for package hBayesDM: is(module, "character"): object 'm' not found Error: loading failed Execution halted ERROR: loading failed

  • removing ‘/private/var/folders/jb/3202zzgd5j304l5pb6yv4_6w0000gn/T/RtmpqAC81F/hBayesDM.Rcheck/hBayesDM’

This error might be critical? error in load action .__A__.1 for package hBayesDM: is(module, "character"): object 'm' not found


Even with the error above, I can install the package: by installing the package directly from GitHub or using the command like 'R CMD INSTALL hBayesDM'.




3. To include precompiled models, I used the Ben Goodrich's suggestion in this post (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/iBjP4Qq7aP4). Now each model's *.rds file is in the '/exec' folder along with *.stan files. I'm not sure if this is the best practice for including precompiled models. Any suggestions/recommendations would be highly appreciated. 




These are some of the posts I found from the Stan mailing list. 

1. https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/GlobalEnv$20core%7Csort:relevance/stan-users/tyD6maC7RRg/cWUNHzIGBQAJ

2. https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/GlobalEnv%7Csort:relevance/stan-users/P-kZHokKg3c/I6ZHHP5mAAAJ

3. https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/JlYv7Rt6-zM



I know there are several things that need to be improved in the package and it would be great if Stan developers can help. Thanks a lot for your help in advance and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Best,
Young Ahn

Hi Ben,

I have a follow-up question. All codes seem to run perfectly fine except this:

after running a model and use hBayesDM function called 'printFit', I get the following error message.


library(hBayesDM)

output = dd_exp("example", 2000, 1000, 4, 4)

printFit(output)


Error in loo::extract_log_lik(stanfit = stanFit, parameter_name = "log_lik") : 

  Please load the 'rstan' package.



If I load rstan (e.g., library(rsatn)) or add 'rstan' to 'Depends', it works fine but I hope to avoid loading the whole package. Any suggestions will be appreciated. 

Best,
Young

On Friday, January 20, 2017 at 2:48:21 PM UTC-5, Young Ahn wrote:
I have a follow-up question. All codes seem to run perfectly fine except this:

after running a model and use hBayesDM function called 'printFit', I get the following error message.


library(hBayesDM)

output = dd_exp("example", 2000, 1000, 4, 4)

printFit(output)


Error in loo::extract_log_lik(stanfit = stanFit, parameter_name = "log_lik") : 

  Please load the 'rstan' package.

It is a bug in loo that has been fixed on github

https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/commit/59ef0e9d79304f9e834100668537db99eff50490

You could work around it for now by including

#' @importFrom rstan rstan_options

Ben
